create.name: European Institute of Applied Buddhism (EIAB)
create.bio:
The European Institute of Applied Buddhism is a monastery and retreat centre of the Plum Village tradition of Thich Nhat Hanh in Waldbröl, a small town east of Cologne in Germany. A resident community of monks and nuns, with Thay Phap An among its senior teachers, runs a year-round programme of weekend and week-long retreats in German, English and Vietnamese, aimed at bringing the Buddha's teachings into everyday life through mindful breathing, walking, working and listening.

Courses at the institute cover topics such as understanding oneself and others, mindfulness at work and the study of the mindfulness trainings, alongside calligraphy, tai chi and qigong practice days. For people further away it offers a free online morning meditation every day and a monthly online day of mindfulness, both run on a donation basis. Its YouTube channel, the EIAB Sangha, began in 2020 and keeps recordings of Dharma talks and guided meditations from the major festivals, New Year's Eve and Vesak celebrations, as well as chanting and ceremonies, many in Vietnamese.

courses.title: Mich selbst und andere verstehen - Understanding myself and others
courses.description: A weekend retreat in German and English on looking into our own feelings, thoughts and motives as a way to live with more understanding of ourselves and others.

courses.title: Arbeit als freudvolles, achtsames Tun erleben – Achtsamkeit in den Alltag bringen
courses.description: A six-day German-language retreat treating work in the house and garden as spiritual practice, led by two of the nuns with the monastic community.

free_resources.title: Online morning meditation
free_resources.description: A free half-hour session on Zoom every morning at 7am: guided or silent sitting, a short reading and a chant to Avalokiteshvara.

free_resources.title: Online day of mindfulness
free_resources.description: A monthly Sunday of practice online, free to join with donations welcome, led by lay members of the community.
